currentContext.strengths: Global branded specialty innovation model — Ryaltris®, Glenmark's first globally launched branded specialty product, scaled through proprietary R&D plus a partnership-led commercialization model to 56 countries, ranking among the top 3 brands in 17 markets and #1 in 5 markets.|Proprietary biologics/multispecific-antibody R&D platform (IGI's BEAT® protein platform), validated externally by a landmark licensing agreement with AbbVie for ISB 2001 (USD 700 Mn upfront; potential aggregate deal value USD 1.925 Bn).|Diversified, balanced geographic and therapy-area mix (India, North America, Europe, Emerging Markets; Dermatology, Respiratory, Oncology, Cardiac, Diabetes) that reduces dependence on any single market or therapy.|Strong brand equity and market position in India — ranked 2nd in Dermatology, 3rd in Respiratory and 4th in Cardiac (IQVIA MAT Mar'26), with 11 brands among the IPM Top 300 and secondary-sales growth consistently outperforming the IPM.|Broad R&D infrastructure of six centres (Sinnar, Taloja, Mahape, Lausanne, New York, Neuchâtel) supporting a pipeline spanning specialty branded products, generics and biologics.
currentContext.strategies: Moving up the value chain through leadership in three global therapeutic areas — Dermatology, Respiratory, and Oncology — by scaling differentiated products, expanding specialty platforms, and advancing proprietary and partnered innovation.|Advancing innovation and specialty: continuing to scale proprietary innovation (Ryaltris®) globally, expanding the innovative Oncology portfolio across India and Emerging Markets through partnerships, building Specialty Dermatology and Respiratory portfolios across Europe, and continuing investment in IGI's proprietary BEAT® platform for next-generation multispecific antibodies.|Scaling the branded business: increasing the contribution of branded markets and products — strengthening the branded business in India, expanding scale across Emerging Markets through deeper penetration and regional brands, and increasing branded/specialty contribution in Europe led by Respiratory and Dermatology.|Building a generics business: scaling the U.S. generics business through Respiratory and Injectable launches, expanding the U.S. Injectables portfolio across hospital/institutional channels, pursuing selective first-to-file opportunities, and gaining scale in Europe generics while progressively increasing higher-value product contribution.|Nurturing sustainability: embedding sustainability into operations and growth, advancing SBTi validation, TNFD disclosure, human rights and workplace culture, and integrating environmental/social considerations into business decisions.|Creating sustainable shareholder value: driving profitable growth and superior returns through disciplined capital allocation, portfolio enhancement, and operating leverage; prioritizing growth initiatives with shorter payback periods; maintaining working capital structurally below the industry average; and pursuing selective, ROCE-gated CAPEX and M&A.|Expanding strategic partnerships across the innovation lifecycle — in-licensing differentiated therapies to strengthen priority therapeutic areas, and partnering IGI-originated innovation with global biopharmaceutical leaders to accelerate development, expand reach and unlock pipeline value.|Oncology franchise build-out: scaling the oncology franchise across India and Emerging Markets through innovative product launches and stronger commercial capabilities, and advancing next-generation oncology innovation through IGI's multispecific pipeline.|Respiratory strategy: scaling Ryaltris® as a global growth platform, strengthening the respiratory portfolio across Europe and North America, and building U.S. leadership through differentiated respiratory generics and device-led capabilities.|Dermatology strategy: sustaining leadership in India and Emerging Markets while expanding into higher-value specialty opportunities, scaling Winlevi® across Europe, and strengthening prescription and OTC/DTC dermatology portfolios in select markets.|Capital allocation decisions — including annual operating plans, business strategies, capital expenditure proposals and quarterly/half-yearly/annual financial results — are reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors, with the Audit Committee reviewing financial statements and key financial reporting matters before Board consideration. Dividend recommendations are approved by the Board and put to a shareholder vote at the AGM; a dividend of INR 2.50 per equity share for FY2026 was placed before Members for approval at the 48th AGM.
currentContext.expansion: North America: continued build-out of the injectable portfolio (more than 20 injectable products launched to date), first-to-market Respiratory generic launches (first to launch the generic version of FloVent® 44 mcg in the U.S.), and an OTC private-label business expanded to seven clients in FY2026. Europe: direct commercial presence expanded to 13 markets with 8 new Respiratory product launches in FY2026, and the launch of Winlevi® (Glenmark's first New Chemical Entity) in the UK followed by EU marketing authorization, providing a platform for further expansion across Glenmark's licensed European territories in FY2027. Emerging Markets: Glenmark is building front-end commercial capabilities across the region to support future commercialization of differentiated Oncology assets. Site-level environmental capex: renewable-energy Power Purchase Agreements (PPA) implemented at the Nashik and CSN sites, and a transition from fossil fuel to biofuel for boiler operations at the Indore site.
currentContext.mdna: Global medicines market projected to grow at 5-8% CAGR through 2030 (exceeding USD 2.6 Tn), supported by sustained innovation despite pricing pressures, healthcare reforms and a significant patent expiry wave; the U.S. is expected to remain the largest contributor to global pharmaceutical market growth.|Oncology is expected to remain the largest therapy area by spending (8-10% CAGR 2026-2030); Obesity is projected to be the fastest-growing therapy area (13-14% CAGR) on GLP-1 adoption; Immunology, Ophthalmology and CNS are also flagged as continuing growth areas relevant to Glenmark's core therapy exposure.|India is expected to remain among the world's fastest-growing major economies (GDP +6.6% in FY2027); reduction in GST rates is expected to support consumer spending even as elevated energy prices and input costs moderate private demand.|Indian pharmaceutical market: domestic market valued at USD 60 Bn, projected to reach USD 130 Bn by FY2030; India supplies around 20% of the world's generic medicines and ~60% of UNICEF's vaccine requirements; government PLI Schemes and the Bulk Drug Parks Scheme continue to support domestic manufacturing capability.|India business demand: underlying demand profile remained strong through FY2026 despite a pronounced one-time sales impact in Q2 FY2026 from the GST regime change; India formulation business significantly outperformed the IPM in secondary sales every quarter, with sustained strength in Cardiac, Dermatology and Respiratory, growing at ~1.5x IPM growth and ranking as the second-fastest-growing company among the top 15 in FY2026.|North America growth driver: increasing focus on Respiratory, Injectables and institutional products where complexity and execution can differentiate, supported by continued progress in strengthening manufacturing and supply capabilities, including the Monroe, North Carolina facility's FDA clearance to restart commercial manufacturing.|Europe growth driver: evolution toward greater contribution from branded and differentiated products, illustrated by the progress of Winlevi® and continued expansion of Ryaltris® across established commercial infrastructure.|Emerging Markets growth driver: broad commercial footprint, local market understanding and longstanding customer relationships supporting expansion of both Glenmark-originated and partnered therapies.|IGI multispecific/proprietary pipeline: ISB 2001 (ABBV-2001, licensed to AbbVie) for Oncology and autoimmune disease; next-wave programs referenced include ISB 880 (LAD191) in Immunology, and partnered programs Telazorlimab (ISB 830) and ISB 830-X8 (STAR-0310).|Oncology partnered/in-licensed pipeline: Tevimbra® (Tislelizumab), Brukinsa® (Zanubrutinib), Aumolertinib, Trastuzumab Rezetecan, Envafolimab, and Akynzeo® (Netupitant/Palonosetron) for cancer supportive care.|Dermatology partnered pipeline: Winlevi® (Clascoterone) and Jabryus® (Abrocitinib) for Atopic Dermatitis.|Respiratory partnered pipeline: Pulmicort® (Budesonide) for Asthma/COPD, Eklira® (Aclidinium Bromide) and Duaklir® (Aclidinium Bromide and Formoterol Fumarate Dihydrate).

risks.risk: Pharmaceutical R&D and pipeline execution risk
risks.note: The AR flags the 'inherent uncertainty associated with pharmaceutical R&D' as a key risk (categorized as Financial Risk, Strategic Risk): the discovery-to-commercialization journey is lengthy and involves scientific, regulatory, manufacturing and commercial challenges at every stage, and not all development programs will achieve regulatory approval or commercial success, which may affect future revenue generation.

Ensuring product quality across manufacturing, packaging, labeling and distribution is identified as essential to consumer trust and brand reputation; the AR states that any instance of failure in product quality would have serious repercussions, particularly as the Company introduces new products and expands into new markets (categorized as Quality Risk).

Glenmark USA continued to defend multiple antitrust and consumer protection lawsuits relating to industry-wide allegations of price-fixing, market allocation and related conduct; it agreed to separate settlements of USD 37.75 Mn with the putative direct purchaser class and USD 29.63 Mn with state attorneys general (the latter payable in annual installments over five years), subject to court approval, while denying the underlying allegations.

risks.risk: U.S. FDA regulatory and manufacturing-site inspection risk
risks.note: The Monroe, North Carolina formulations facility required a U.S. FDA Establishment Inspection Report before commercial manufacturing could restart (resolved with a Voluntary Action Indicated classification in November 2025), illustrating exposure to FDA site-inspection outcomes. As of March 31, 2026 the Company also had 52 applications pending at various stages of the U.S. FDA approval process, including 25 Paragraph IV applications, an unresolved regulatory-approval pipeline.

risks.risk: Geopolitical and demand-volatility exposure in Emerging Markets
risks.note: Emerging Markets (Russia/CIS, LATAM, MEA, APAC) performance in FY2026 was affected by seasonal demand patterns, geopolitical uncertainties and delayed launches in selected markets, particularly in the first half, indicating structural exposure to geopolitical and macro volatility across the Company's international footprint.

The August 2025 GST regime change caused a pronounced one-time impact to India formulation sales in Q2 FY2026, contributing to a reported 17.0% decline in India business revenue for FY2026 despite strong underlying secondary-sales demand, showing sensitivity to domestic tax-policy transitions.

Glenmark's risk governance disclosure states that, as a pharmaceutical company with a global geographic footprint, it is 'inherently exposed to a diverse set of risks including geopolitical complexity and scientific advancements,' managed through an Enterprise Risk Management Framework overseen by the Board's Risk Management Committee.

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.
